column7: Three gaps, all measured. (1) ORG has one setting per department, as Ilaria predicted: we need ORG allowed for public bank and shipping-line names and masked for the client (E1). (2) FALSE NEGATIVE: the surname-first form 'DE VRIES, Jan' was not detected at all and reached the cloud model verbatim, while 'Jan de Vries', 'J. de Vries' and 'Jan' were caught in the same prompt (T3 FAIL). (3) Tokens are per surface form, not per identity: one person received PERSON_REF_1 and PERSON_REF_2 in a single prompt, so an identity-reconciliation task cannot be answered correctly even when protection works. (4) OVER-DETECTION CORRUPTS THE PROMPT: at piiSensitivity high, BRANE labelled the ordinary phrases 'expiry on' and 'Beneficiary' as PERSON and substituted them, so the cloud model received 'before the instrument PERSON_REF_2 2027-01-31' and 'PERSON_REF_3 ORG_DEMO_02 disputes the treatment of discrepancies'. Three words were deleted from a five-sentence case note; earlier the span 'confirms SIGNATORY_1' removed the verb. Routing was correct every time, the content was not, and no header reports it (T3c FAIL). What is needed is a per-category confidence floor, or an allowlist of business vocabulary the name detector must not claim.

column7: Ilaria's predicted gap is confirmed and is worse than stated: rules apply per department, not per task, so 'refuse in commercial drafting but local in a Compliance classification step' is inexpressible. Measured on top of that: a category set to local protects nothing if the detector never applies the label, and BRANE offers no confidence threshold, no 'route local when merely suspected', and no way to require that a category must match before a turn may go to cloud. BRANE also silently truncates a semantic rule's keyword list at 20 entries and still returns HTTP 200.
